title: From Auction Table to Playing XI: How Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s Squad Philosophy Evolved
dek: How Royal Challengers Bengaluru build a squad, and how much of it they actually use, has changed across their history. Squad lists show the shift from auction table to playing eleven.
excerpt: Royal Challengers Bengaluru have used less of their squad since 2024 than in 2008–2023. Squad size and usage are the clearest record of a franchise's squad philosophy.

sections.heading: Squads Are Philosophies
body: A squad list records a philosophy: how many specialists, how much cover, how many young players to carry. How much of the squad gets used shows whether the plan trusted depth or a fixed eleven.

The impact-player rule, introduced in 2023, gives each side an extra player per match, which tends to widen squad usage across the league.

sections.heading: Philosophy or Circumstance?
body: Usage also rises with injuries and poor form, so a wider spread is not always a plan.

sections.heading: Limits of the Squad Lists
body: Squad lists are compiled from public sources and include known errors in roles and nationalities. Squad size and the played flag are the most reliable fields.
Mid-season replacements are included when the lists record them.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: A Tighter Core
body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru have relied on a tighter core since 2024 compared with 2008–2023.
Comparing that shift with other franchises would show whether it reflects a choice or the rule change.
